tasks.short: Develop design solutions with creative directors

steps.what: Send constraints and the job for a design
Draft design solutions from those constraints

loop.input: constraint fields and the solution template
loop.output: two solutions each citing a constraint id
loop.check: Every solution names a constraint id from the form
loop.stop: One pass, then stop; leave a blank if a solution has no constraint id
loop.why_not_simpler: The wording of a direction is not a fixed lookup

steps.what: Develop the design with the creative directors
File the design solution agreed in the session

tasks.design: Creative directors submit job id, audience, constraint and deadline on a {PROJECT} form. A bounded draft in {DOCS} proposes design solutions that cite those fields, and a generated frame is not the agreed solution. The art director develops the solution with the creative directors, then files that internal version in {DOCS} with content-credential metadata.
tasks.previous_blocker: Constraints lived in mail and sketch notes, so a draft could not show which limit it was answering.
tasks.enabler_now: The job form can share one job id with the draft, so each proposal can be checked against a field.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a direction with the creative directors is a live conversation, not a score.
tasks.human_edge: The art director decides which design solution the session will stand behind.

ambition.what: Agree the design solution at the end of each working session, not only when a campaign is already late

tasks.altitude: Less time rewriting the brief, the same weight on the session. The art director can refuse a draft that cites no constraint.

reach.task: Take the agreed design solution into the next creative review
reach.learn: Which solution was agreed and which constraints were dropped

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm this task is a working session. The hard part is the direction, not the formatting of the note.

Digest [S2] and [S3] describe a design tool that drafts from a prompt and a campaign-layout tool that fills locked areas. A person still approves the layout. A generated frame is not the approved design.
Digest [S8] is a commentary that generative tools change craft and that a person still directs the work. It is not a measured saving.
Digest [S1] says content-credential metadata can be attached to a creative file. That is metadata, not a judgement that the layout is good.
Digest [S12], [S13] and [S14] say copyright in a model-made logo or image is unsettled. The art director does not treat a generated image as owned.

assumptions: Focal role is the art director. The task ends when the internal design solution is filed. Presenting it to a client is a later task, and nothing is published here.

Input contract: job id, audience, constraint text, deadline, brand rule id. Producer is the creative director. If the form is empty the art director types the same fields from mail and marks the row manual.
Use the document store's own templates before custom code. A model-made image in the draft is not owned and is not cleared for external use.
unknowns: Who may agree a solution when the art director is absent.
Whether brand rules already exist as fields.
research_questions: How often does the session reject every drafted solution?
Which constraints arrive only as mail?

already_counted.description: Art director edits weak solutions before the session
Working-session time with creative directors stays

incremental.description: Keep the solution template aligned with new constraint fields
Creative directors correct constraints the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: design solution agreed in this session

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes half the jobs still arrive as free-text mail, so the art director retypes constraints. The high case assumes the form is used but the working session still happens in full. Client presentation is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Present final layouts to clients for approval

steps.what: Assemble final layouts and the approval set
Clear rights and marks before clients see layouts
Present the final layouts in the client meeting
Record the clients' approval of these layouts
File the layouts version the clients approved

tasks.design: The art director assembles final layouts in {DOCS} from the signed spec. Before the meeting, the art director clears rights and confirms that any model-made image or video carries a synthetic-media mark. The client approves one version in the room, and only that version is filed to {CMS} and noted by {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approvals came back as mail threads, so a file step could not know which layout version the client had seen.
tasks.enabler_now: Each layout can carry a version id, a mark status and a rights status that the pack can check.
tasks.still_hard: The client can still reject the work in the room for reasons that are not on the form.
tasks.human_edge: The client decides whether these layouts are approved. The art director does not file a version the client did not accept.

ambition.what: Record a client layout approval at the presentation, not only when a yes arrives later by mail

tasks.altitude: Pack-building shrinks. The presentation and the client's approval stay. The art director can refuse to show a file with a blank mark or a blank rights field.

reach.task: Make only the layout version the client approved
reach.learn: Which version was approved and whether the mark was confirmed

evidence.claim: Presenting layouts is a meeting. The part that can move is assembling the pack and filing the version the client named.
Digest [S9] and [S10] describe EU transparency duties for synthetic media. A published image or video that a model made is marked as such before it goes out, and a person confirms the mark.
Digest [S11] reports that campaign images often omit that synthetic-media mark. The mark check is mandatory in this design.
Digest [S12], [S13] and [S14] say copyright in a model-made image is unsettled. A person clears rights before external use, and the art director does not treat a generated image as owned.

assumptions: Focal role is the art director. The task runs from a signed spec to a filed client decision. Making the layout is a different task.

Input contract: layout id, version, client id, model-made yes or no, mark status, rights status. Producer is the art director from the signed spec. If mark status or rights status is blank, the pack is not presented and the art director fills the field by hand.
Use the asset store's own version and approval fields before custom code. The meeting itself is not replaced by a form.
unknowns: Whether this client will approve in the room or only later in writing.
Who may present when the art director is away.
research_questions: How often is a layout shown with no version id?
How often does the client approve a different version from the one in the pack?

already_counted.description: Art director still checks rights and marks before the meeting
Presentation time in the client meeting stays

incremental.description: Keep mark and rights fields aligned with new file types
Clients resend a decision when the version id was wrong

approvals.approved_version: layouts pack with rights cleared and marks confirmed
client approval of this layouts version
the layouts version named in that client approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many layouts still have no version id, so the art director rebuilds the pack by hand. The high case assumes clean files but the presentation and the client decision still take their full time. The client's travel and the later print run are not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Manage accounts, projects, budget and scheduling

steps.what: Read accounts, budget and scheduling requirements
Flag projects that miss those scheduling requirements
Decide which projects stay within budget
Update project dates from the signed decision
Talk through the scheduling change with the account

tasks.design: Account id, project id, budget, spent, deadline and owner sit on a {SPREADSHEET} tied to {PROJECT}. A view flags projects outside budget or scheduling requirements. The art director decides what slips, the {PROJECT} dates update only from that decision, and the change is talked through by {EMAIL} or a short call.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budget and dates were split across mail and private notes, so a flag could not tell a real slip from a stale row.
tasks.enabler_now: The tracker can hold budget, spent and deadline on one project id.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing which project slips is a judgement about the client, not a threshold.
tasks.human_edge: The art director decides which projects stay within budget and which dates move.

ambition.what: Review account budget and scheduling slips every week, not only at month end

tasks.altitude: Scanning the sheet shrinks. The slip decision and the conversation about it stay. The art director can block a date change that has no signed decision.

reach.task: Replan a job around the signed schedule
reach.learn: Which projects slipped and which budget row caused it

evidence.claim: Account control in a mid-size studio is a tracker plus a conversation. The dates and the budget can be compared by rule. The slip decision cannot.

assumptions: Focal role is the art director. The task is the art director's own accounts and projects, not the company forecast.

Input contract: account id, project id, budget amount, spent amount, deadline, owner. Producer is the art director when the job is opened. If a row has no project id the art director types it from mail and marks the row manual.
Configure the tracker views and required fields before any custom code. The meeting prior is the scheduling conversation, not a design review.
unknowns: Whether budget figures are allowed to sit outside the finance system.
Who may move a date when the art director is away.
research_questions: What share of projects has no owner or no deadline?
How often does the weekly flag list change a date?

already_counted.description: Art director's slip decisions stay inside the review
The scheduling conversation stays with the art director

incremental.description: Add a field when a new account type appears on the tracker

approvals.approved_version: schedule decision for these project ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many accounts still arrive as mail, so the art director retypes budget rows. The high case assumes the sheet is current but every slip still needs a decision and a conversation. Chasing a client for money is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with department heads on creative work

steps.what: Send client requirements and presentation concepts
Order the concepts into a conference agenda
Confer with department heads on creative activities
Coordinate which creative activities go forward
File the activity list from that conference

tasks.design: Department heads send client requirements and presentation concepts by {EMAIL} onto a {PROJECT} agenda. The art director confers with them and coordinates creative activities. The agreed activity list is filed in {DOCS}. The conference itself stays in the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrived as separate threads, so the conference started by reconstructing the agenda.
tasks.enabler_now: A shared agenda can list requirement, concept and owner before the meeting.
tasks.still_hard: Coordinating people who disagree is still a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The art director decides which creative activities go forward after the conference.

ambition.what: Confirm creative activities at each conference instead of leaving them open in mail

tasks.altitude: Agenda gathering shrinks. The conference stays. The art director can refuse to close the list while a named requirement has no owner.

reach.task: Write to the concepts the conference kept
reach.learn: Which presentation concepts were kept and which activities are still open

evidence.claim: This is a daily conference. A prepared agenda helps. It does not replace the talk among department heads.

assumptions: Focal role is the art director. The task ends when the activity list is filed. Doing the creative work is a later task.

Input contract: department, client requirement, presentation concept, owner, meeting date. Producer is the department head. If the form is empty the art director types the points in the room and marks them manual.
Use the project board's own agenda fields before custom code. The design does not watch staff at work.
unknowns: Which departments must attend before a list can close.
Whether copy and production share one board.
research_questions: How often does the conference start with no written requirements?
How many activities leave the room with no owner?

already_counted.description: Conference time with department heads stays
The activity decision at the end of the conference stays

incremental.description: Adjust agenda fields when a new department joins the conference
Department heads resubmit requirements the agenda rejects

approvals.approved_version: activity list agreed in this conference

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes heads still send free-text mail, so the art director builds the agenda by hand. The high case assumes a clean agenda but the conference and the activity decision still take their full time. The work the activities point at is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week keeps the creative-director session, the client approval and the department conference, and moves pack-building, mark checks and account flags out of the meeting.
reach: Creative directors receive the filed design solution instead of a recap in mail.
Production heads receive only the layout version the client approved.
Department heads can read the activity list without asking which ideas survived.
skills_to_grow: Write a design constraint as a field a draft can cite.
Separate a client approval from the act of filing the layout.
Keep budget and scheduling dates in one tracker.
role.ambitious_version: Each account has a current budget row, and no layout reaches a client without a confirmed mark and a recorded approval.
